card.description:
Overview:

QXO is a leading distributor and installer of building products serving an $800 billion market. The company’s mission is to modernize the building products industry through advanced technology and a best-in-class customer experience. QXO is North America’s largest distributor and installer of insulation, the second-largest distributor of roofing products, the second-largest publicly traded distributor of lumber and building materials, and the largest distributor of waterproofing products. The company is targeting $50 billion in annual revenue within the decade through accretive acquisitions and organic growth. For more information, visit QXO.com.

What you will do::

As the Plant Manager, you will serve as the senior leader of the operation, with full responsibility for the facility's operational performance, customer experience, employee engagement, and financial results. You will lead a truss manufacturing business serving residential, commercial, multifamily, and agricultural construction markets while driving profitable growth, operational excellence, and a culture centered on safety, accountability, and continuous improvement.

In this role, you will:

* Assume full P&L responsibility for the business, including revenue growth, gross margin performance, operating expenses, EBITDA, and overall profitability.
* Develop and execute business plans that drive market share growth, operational efficiency, customer satisfaction, and financial performance.
* Lead all day-to-day operations of the truss manufacturing facility, including production, engineering/design, purchasing, scheduling, inventory, logistics, maintenance, and quality.
* Partner with sales leadership to drive revenue growth, strengthen customer relationships, expand market opportunities, and improve competitive positioning.
* Analyze financial and operational performance metrics, identify trends, and implement action plans that improve profitability and business results.
* Maintain accountability for budgeting, forecasting, cost management, capital expenditures, working capital, and inventory performance.
* Lead and develop supervisors, managers, and frontline team members while creating a high-performance culture focused on accountability and results.
* Champion safety, quality, and continuous improvement initiatives across all aspects of the operation.
* Ensure production capacity, staffing, and operational resources are aligned with customer demand and growth objectives.
* Foster strong relationships with contractors, builders, developers, architects, engineers, suppliers, and internal stakeholders.
* Lead change management initiatives, process improvements, and strategic projects that enhance operational performance and long-term scalability.
* Serve as the primary business leader for the operation, balancing customer needs, employee development, operational execution, and financial performance.

What you will bring::

* 7+ years of progressive leadership experience in truss manufacturing, engineered wood products, building materials, lumber, component manufacturing, construction products, or a related industry.
* Proven success leading a manufacturing operation with direct P&L ownership and accountability for revenue, margin, and profitability.
* Strong business acumen with experience managing budgets, forecasting, cost controls, pricing strategies, capital investments, and financial performance.
* Experience driving profitable growth through operational improvements, sales partnership, customer development, and market expansion.
* Demonstrated ability to lead cross-functional teams including operations, production, purchasing, engineering/design, logistics, and customer-facing functions.
* Strong understanding of manufacturing KPIs, labor productivity, inventory management, throughput optimization, and supply chain operations.
* Experience building high-performing teams and developing future leaders.
* Proven ability to make data-driven business decisions and execute strategic initiatives.
* Excellent communication, relationship-building, and leadership skills.

**Success in This Role**

The ideal candidate combines the mindset of a business leader with the execution skills of an operations leader. This individual will take ownership of the entire operation, drive sustainable revenue and profitability growth, strengthen customer relationships, improve operational performance, and build an engaged, high-performing team. Success will be measured by the operation's safety performance, customer satisfaction, employee engagement, operational efficiency, revenue growth, and overall financial results.

What you will earn::

* 401(k) with employer match
* Medical, dental, and vision insurance
* PTO, company holidays, and parental leave
* Paid training and certifications
* Legal assistance and identity protection
* Pet insurance
* Employee assistance program (EAP)

**QXO is an Equal Opportunity Employer**. *It is the policy of the Company to comply with all employment laws and to afford equal employment opportunity to individuals in all aspects of employment, including in selection for job opportunities, without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, pregnancy, national origin, age, disability, genetic information, military service, protected veteran status, or any other consideration protected by federal, state or local laws.*

*If you are an individual with a disability and need assistance submitting an application or would like to request an accommodation, please email us at careers@QXO.com to make a request.*

card.title: Industrial Engineering, Sr Manager - Operational Excellence
card.description:
**Entity:** CSL Behring

**Job Category:** Business Process Excellence

**Job Family:** Business Process Management

**Job Type:** Full Time

**Location****:** Kankakee, Illinois, United States

**Employer Reference:** R-295434

**Job Description**
-------------------

**Serve as the site Industrial Engineering subject matter expert and strategic owner for labor modeling governance, workforce planning, and productivity improvement across site operations. The role establishes and maintains site-wide standards, models, assumptions, and governance that connect workload, flow, capacity, staffing, labor hours, and cost; advises Site Senior Leadership on workforce strategy and long-range planning; and owns the analytical framework used to identify, prioritize, and validate productivity opportunities. The role also provides broader industrial engineering leadership for manufacturing-system design, capacity analysis, operational readiness, and continuous improvement while protecting safety, quality, service, reliability, and end-to-end performance.**

 
 

Role that this position reports to: Operational Excellence Site Lead

 
 

**Main Responsibilities and Accountabilities**

1. **Site Labor Modeling Governance and Workforce Strategy:**

* Own the site-wide labor modeling framework and governance, including the standards, methods, assumptions, and decision rules used to translate workload into staffing requirements.
* Distinguish direct, indirect, fixed, variable, and workload-driven labor so staffing decisions are based on the appropriate demand mechanism rather than historical headcount alone.
* Build scenario capability for changes in demand, mix, operating calendar, shift structure, automation, productivity, and capacity assumptions.
* Establish and enforce requirements for source data, calculation logic, assumptions, version control, model ownership, review, and approval.
* Compare modeled labor requirements with actual staffing, paid hours, and performance; explain material variance using workload, coverage, process, and structural drivers.
* Advise Site Senior Leadership on workforce strategy and long-range planning, and provide authoritative labor assumptions for budget cycles, productivity commitments, operating changes, and investment decisions.

2. **Productivity Analysis and Opportunity Development:**

* Develop productivity views that connect labor hours and cost to output, workload, service levels, and value-stream performance.
* Identify productivity opportunities through work measurement, flow analysis, staffing alignment, standard work, workload elimination, role clarity, schedule design, process simplification, digital enablement, and automation where justified.
* Prioritize opportunities based on verified business impact, implementation effort, risk, and effect on system performance rather than local utilization alone.
* Quantify baseline, expected benefit, implementation timing, and sustainment measures before an opportunity is counted as productivity.
* Partner with Finance and functional owners to validate benefit logic, establish ownership, and prevent double counting.
* Own the site-wide pipeline and governance for quantified productivity opportunities across manufacturing and support functions, including prioritization, benefit validation, ownership, and status visibility.

3. **Site Productivity Governance, Delivery, and Sustainment:**

* Lead or support productivity projects where Industrial Engineering analysis, work measurement, or operating-model design is required.
* Establish and own site standards for labor modeling, time study, staffing analysis, capacity analysis, and productivity-benefit validation.
* Use observed performance and structured loss data to distinguish demand, staffing, process, equipment, and management-system problems.
* Ensure proposed labor changes do not transfer work, create hidden overtime, increase WIP, reduce quality or reliability, or shift constraints elsewhere.
* Own site-level reporting and decision support that shows required labor, actual labor, productivity gap, root driver, actions, realized benefit, and remaining opportunity.
* Hold the governance process for consistent use of models and standards, and enable operational and functional leaders to embed the capability in the business.

4. **Manufacturing Systems, Flow, and Capacity Analysis:**

* Develop and maintain process, flow, and capacity models for existing operations, expansions, new products, technology transfers, and other significant operating changes.
* Analyze material flow, personnel flow, WIP, buffers, staging, handoffs, resource requirements, and key information flows.
* Challenge capacity and resource assumptions using required rate, product mix, routing, cycle time, changeover, eligible operating time, demonstrated performance, and planned losses.
* Review layouts and process concepts for operability, flow, ergonomics, maintainability, and avoidance of unnecessary transport, motion, waiting, and inventory.
* Identify likely system constraints and distinguish throughput constraints from local performance gaps.
* Translate analysis into clear recommendations for equipment, staffing, shift patterns, skills, space, and operating controls, and present material implications to Site Senior Leadership.

5. **Operational Readiness and Cross-Functional Support:**

* Provide Industrial Engineering support during equipment selection, installation, commissioning, qualification, startup, and operational handoff where decisions affect flow, capacity, labor, or operability.
* Define the operating assumptions and performance measures that should be confirmed during implementation and startup.
* Compare demonstrated cycle time, throughput, utilization, staffing, labor content, WIP, and process performance against approved models.
* Identify gaps between design intent and actual performance and support targeted corrective action.
* Support practical standard work, visual controls, staffing logic, baseline performance measures, and operating handoffs.
* Partner across Engineering, Manufacturing, Quality, Supply Chain, Finance, Digital, Automation, and other functions to support business priorities.
 

 

Qualifications:

 

**Education**

* Bachelor's degree in Industrial Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, Systems Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, or related technical discipline.

* Master's degree in Engineering, Operations Management, Business Administration, Analytics, or related field considered a plus.

* Lean Six Sigma certification preferred.

 
 

**Experience**

* 7+ years of experience in manufacturing, operations, industrial engineering, workforce planning, productivity, or a related analytical role.

* Demonstrated experience with labor modeling, capacity modeling, work measurement, productivity analysis, process improvement, or manufacturing-systems design.

* Experience using operational data to build models, test assumptions, evaluate scenarios, and support business decisions.

* Demonstrated experience establishing site-wide standards or governance, advising senior leaders, and influencing strategic decisions without direct authority.

* Experience in pharmaceutical, biotechnology, medical-device, food, chemical, consumer-products, or other regulated or complex manufacturing environments is preferred.

* Experience supporting capital projects, facility startup, operational readiness, automation, or major operating changes is considered a plus.

 
 

**Competencies**

* Industrial Engineering: flow, capacity, work measurement, labor standards, staffing models, and systems thinking.

* Data and Analytics: ability to translate operational data into clear models, assumptions, scenarios, and decisions.

* Operational Excellence: Lean principles, structured problem solving, standard work, visual management, and continuous improvement.

* Business Acumen: understanding of manufacturing cost, labor economics, capital tradeoffs, and productivity value.

* Strategic and Change Leadership: ability to own site-wide governance, advise senior leadership, and align Engineering, Manufacturing, Quality, Supply Chain, Finance, Digital, and Automation around common workforce and productivity decisions.

* Executive Communication: ability to translate technical models, assumptions, risks, and recommendations into clear decisions for operators, managers, and Site Senior Leadership.

* Judgment: willingness to challenge assumptions, distinguish local performance from system constraints, and focus effort on material business impact.

 
 

**Environment**

* Candidate must be able to wear clean room garments and personal protective equipment and meet cGMP gowning requirements to work in manufacturing environments. Work environment may include navigating a large facility as well as operating in a production office. Exposure to various temperatures, hazardous chemicals, and potential bloodborne pathogens. May be required to work overtime and extended hours to support business needs. Some travel (<) may be required.

 
 

***The expected base salary range for this position at hiring is $139,000- $164,000. Please note this salary range reflects the minimum and maximum base pay that CSL expects to pay for this position at the listed location as of the time of this posting. Individual base salary for a successful candidate is determined by qualifications, skill level, experience, competencies and other relevant factors. In addition to base salary, total compensation for this role may also include incentive compensation and equity.***

**About CSL Behring**
---------------------

CSL Behring is a global biotherapeutics leader driven by our promise to save lives. Focused on serving patients' needs by using the latest technologies, we discover, develop and deliver innovative therapies for people living with conditions in the immunology, hematology, cardiovascular and metabolic, respiratory, and transplant therapeutic areas. We use three strategic scientific platforms of plasma fractionation, recombinant protein technology, and cell and gene therapy to support continued innovation and continually refine ways in which products can address unmet medical needs and help patients lead full lives.

CSL Behring operates one of the world's largest plasma collection networks, CSL Plasma. Our parent company, CSL, headquartered in Melbourne, Australia, employs 32,000 people, and delivers its lifesaving therapies to people in more than 100 countries.

To learn more about CSL, CSL Behring, CSL Seqirus and CSL Vifor visit https://www.csl.com/ and CSL Plasma at https://www.cslplasma.com/.

**Our Benefits**
----------------

For more information on CSL benefits visit How CSL Supports Your Well-being | CSL.

**You Belong at CSL**
---------------------

At CSL, Inclusion and Belonging is at the core of our mission and who we are. It fuels our innovation day in and day out. By celebrating our differences and creating a culture of curiosity and empathy, we are able to better understand and connect with our patients and donors, foster strong relationships with our stakeholders, and sustain a diverse workforce that will move our company and industry into the future.

To learn more about inclusion and belonging visit https://www.csl.com/careers/inclusion-and-belonging

**Equal Opportunity Employer**
------------------------------

CSL is an Equal Opportunity Employer. If you are an individual with a disability and need a reasonable accommodation for any part of the application process, please visit https://www.csl.com/accessibility-statement.

card.description:
SET THE VISION. LEAD WITH PURPOSE. DRIVE OPERATIONAL EXCELLENCE.

Plant Manager | Full-Time | Salary

AUTOKINITON | Chicago, IL (relocation available)

Are you an experienced manufacturing leader who knows how to bring people together, strengthen operations, and turn business goals into measurable results? At AUTOKINITON, you'll have the opportunity to lead an entire plant, develop future leaders, and drive the safety, quality, productivity, and financial performance that keep our business moving forward.

WHO WE ARE

At AUTOKINITON, our work helps shape the vehicles people drive every day. As a trusted partner to the world's leading automakers, we take pride in building high-quality structural components that contribute to vehicle strength, durability, and safety. But what truly drives our success is our people. Guided by our core value, “We, Not I,” we believe in teamwork, continuous improvement, and creating opportunities for every associate to contribute, grow, and succeed. Join a team where your leadership makes a difference, your ideas drive improvement, and we're building the future of mobility together.

PURPOSE: WHAT YOU'LL DO

As Plant Manager, you'll provide strategic and hands-on leadership across all plant operations, building a strong team while delivering results for our customers and our business.

* Lead Plant Performance: Direct daily operations to achieve safety, quality, productivity, delivery, and financial goals.

* Develop Strong Leaders: Coach, mentor, and develop the leadership team and salaried associates, building accountability and future management talent.

* Drive Business Results: Own plant financial performance, manage budgets and staffing levels, and identify opportunities to improve efficiency and reduce costs.

* Build a Culture of Safety: Lead plant safety initiatives, strengthen EHS accountability, and ensure compliance with company policies and OSHA requirements.

* Improve Operations: Champion lean manufacturing, structured problem-solving, and continuous improvement to increase productivity and eliminate waste.

* Deliver for Customers: Build strong customer relationships, lead customer visits and presentations, and ensure plant performance consistently meets or exceeds expectations.

* Shape the Business Strategy: Develop and execute the plant's strategic business plan, aligning measurable goals with broader North American business objectives.

* Support Growth and Innovation: Partner with commercial, engineering, and program teams on new business opportunities, customer launches, plant capacity, and operational readiness.

* Strengthen Teamwork: Create an engaged, collaborative environment where associates have the resources, direction, and support to succeed.

WHAT MAKES YOU A GREAT FIT?

* Bachelor's degree in Business or a related field; preference for Manufacturing, Engineering, or Quality. Master's degree preferred.

* Minimum of 8-10 years of manufacturing leadership experience as a Plant Manager, Operations Manager, or Department Manager, with metals manufacturing experience preferred, with at least 5 years within a weld and assembly facility.

* Experience with Just-in-Time (JIT) manufacturing, including production scheduling, inventory management, and material flow principles.

* Experience leading new program launches and implementing lean manufacturing principles.

* Proven ability to lead, coach, mentor, and develop high-performing teams.

* Strong business and financial acumen, including the ability to interpret operating metrics and financial performance data.

* Knowledge of quality and environmental management systems, including IATF 16949 and ISO 14001.

* Excellent organizational, analytical, communication, and interpersonal skills.

* Proficiency in Microsoft Office; QAD and supply chain experience preferred.

* Ability to translate business strategies and progressive manufacturing practices into measurable operational improvements.

WHY BUILD YOUR CAREER WITH AUTOKINITON?

* Competitive compensation

* Medical, dental, and vision coverage

* 401(k) company contribution and match

* Up to 15 paid holidays, including our holiday bridge schedule

* Tuition reimbursement

* Professional development, training, and career advancement opportunities

* A collaborative, team-focused culture built on continuous improvement

READY TO LEAD THE WAY?

Bring your leadership experience, business mindset, and passion for manufacturing to AUTOKINITON. Apply today and help drive the future of our business!

AUTOKINITON promotes a dynamic and collaborative work environment for everyone.

AUTOKINITON is an equal opportunity employer that is committed to diversity and inclusion in the workplace. We prohibit discrimination and harassment of any kind based on race, color, sex, religion, sexual orientation, national origin, disability, genetic information, pregnancy, or any other protected characteristic as outlined by federal, state, or local laws.

This policy applies to all employment practices within our organization, including hiring, recruiting, promotion, termination, layoff, recall, leave of absence, compensation, benefits, training, and apprenticeship. AUTOKINITON makes hiring decisions based solely on qualifications, merit, and business needs at the time.

card.description:
**Job Description**
The Senior Manager of Manufacturing Product & Test Engineering is a leadership role responsible for ensuring that products are designed, validated, and manufactured with robust, scalable, and cost-effective test solutions. This leader will lead product engineering, test engineering, and new product introduction (NPI) through mass production activities within manufacturing, ensuring seamless transition from design to high-volume production. The role partners closely with design, quality, and external partners to deliver high-quality, reliable products while optimizing test coverage, yield, and cost.
 
 
**Responsibilities**
**Key Responsibilities**

* Strategic Leadership & Execution

+ Lead NPI readiness and manufacturing ramp strategies to ensure successful product launches.

* Product Engineering

+ Oversee product engineering activities supporting manufacturing, including BOM management, configuration control, and engineering change implementation (ECO/ECN).
+ Ensure design for manufacturability (DFM), design for testability (DFT), and design for reliability (DFR) principles are embedded in product development.
+ Drive root cause analysis and resolution of product-related issues in production and the field.

* Test Engineering & Validation

+ Lead the development and deployment of manufacturing test strategies, including functional, parametric, environmental, and reliability testing.
+ Optimize test coverage, cycle time, and cost while maintaining product quality and compliance.
+ Oversee test equipment design, validation, calibration, and lifecycle management.
+ Implement advanced test technologies, automation, and data analytics to improve efficiency and insight.

* New Product Introduction (NPI)

+ Partner with design to ensure smooth product transfers from development to manufacturing.
+ Establish robust validation processes and pilot builds.
+ Drive readiness reviews, risk assessments, and launch performance tracking.

* Operational Excellence & Continuous Improvement

+ Champion Lean, Six Sigma, and data-driven methodologies to improve yield, throughput, and reliability.
+ Identify and eliminate production inefficiencies and test bottlenecks.
+ Establish KPIs and dashboards for product performance, test efficiency, and manufacturing readiness.

* Cross-Functional Collaboration

+ Collaborate with Quality, Supply Chain, Procurement, and Operations to ensure alignment on product requirements and execution.
+ Support supplier selection and qualification for test equipment and capabilities.
+ Act as a key liaison between engineering and manufacturing teams globally.

* Team Leadership & Development

+ Build, lead, and mentor high-performing product and test engineering teams across multiple locations.
+ Develop organizational capability in advanced test engineering, data analytics, and product support.
+ Drive a culture of innovation, accountability, and continuous learning.

**Qualifications**

* Education & Experience

+ Bachelor’s degree in engineering (Electrical, Computer, or related field); Master’s degree or MBA preferred.
+ 8-10+ years of experience in product engineering or test engineering, with at least 5+ years in a management role.
+ Proven track record supporting complex product portfolios.

* Technical Expertise

+ Deep knowledge of product lifecycle management (PLM), configuration control, and engineering change processes.
+ Strong expertise in manufacturing test methodologies, test system design, and validation processes.
+ Experience with DFM, DFT, DFR, and reliability engineering principles.
+ Familiarity with automation, data acquisition systems, and Industry 4.0 technologies.
+ Background in test automation, software-driven testing, and data analytics platforms.

* Leadership & Business Acumen

+ Strong strategic thinking, problem-solving, and execution capabilities.
+ Financial acumen, including capital planning and cost optimization.
+ Track record of successful product launches and manufacturing scale-ups.

* Skills & Competencies

+ Excellent analytical and troubleshooting skills.
+ Ability to manage complex programs and competing priorities.
+ High level of integrity, accountability, and adaptability.

**Work Environment & Travel**

* Combination of office, lab, and manufacturing environments.
* Travel required (~25%) depending on product lifecycle and location

card.title: Director of Production - Headset and Battery
card.description:
Unusual Machines is a U.S.-based drone and drone parts company focused on the small and First-Person View (FPV) segments of the drone market. Our brands - Rotor Riot, Fat Shark, Rotor Lab and - coming soon - Upgrade Energy - are some of the most respected names in FPV and have helped shape the industry through e-commerce, product development, and a deep connection with the pilot community.
 
 
We’re expanding into enterprise and defense - bringing our obsessive attention to performance, design, and U.S.-based manufacturing into high-stakes environments like search and rescue and military innovation. With several of our products already approved by the Defense Innovation Unit, we’re solving procurement issues for customers who demand speed, agility, and compliance.
 
 
If you love working at the intersection of community, content, and cutting-edge technology, you’ll feel right at home here.
 
 
Director of Production
 
 
**Location:**
Orlando, Florida
 
 
Who You Are
 
 
You are an experienced manufacturing leader who knows how to turn complex hardware into a repeatable, scalable production operation.
 
 
You’re equally comfortable setting the strategy and getting on the production floor to solve problems. You thrive in fast-moving environments, build strong teams, and bring structure, accountability, and continuous improvement to everything you do.
 
 
You have experience leading production of complex hardware—ideally electronics, electromechanical products, batteries, drones, robotics, aerospace, or similar—and understand what it takes to scale from early production to meaningful volume.
 
 
What You’ll Do
 
 

* Own production operations for our FPV headsets, cameras, and renewable/rechargeable battery assemblies in Orlando.
* Build and lead a high-performing production team, including supervisors, leads, specialists, and assembly personnel.
* Establish the processes, systems, staffing, and production standards needed to scale.
* Own production planning, capacity, throughput, quality, yield, labor efficiency, and on-time delivery.
* Develop standardized work, assembly processes, testing procedures, and production KPIs.
* Identify bottlenecks and drive continuous improvement across the production floor.
* Partner closely with Engineering, Quality, Supply Chain, and Product Development to ensure products are designed and built for manufacturing.
* Lead the introduction of new products and processes into production.
* Evaluate tooling, equipment, automation, and capital investments that improve capacity, quality, and cost.
* Build a culture of safety, quality, accountability, and continuous improvement.

What You’ll Bring
 
 

* 8+ years of progressive manufacturing or production leadership experience.
* Experience scaling production operations and building manufacturing teams and processes.
* Strong understanding of Lean Manufacturing, continuous improvement, and production KPIs.
* Experience with complex hardware, electronics, batteries, aerospace, drones, robotics, or similar products preferred.
* Experience with NPI, DFM/DFA, production testing, and manufacturing process development.
* Strong problem-solving, analytical, and organizational skills.
* Experience working with ERP/MRP and production planning systems.
* A hands-on leadership style with the ability to move between strategic planning and solving issues on the production floor.
* A bachelor's degree in engineering, manufacturing, operations, business, or a related field is preferred.

What Does Success Look Like?
 
 
**In Your First 6 Months, You Will**

* Build a strong, accountable battery production organization.
* Establish scalable processes and standardized work across all product lines.
* Create clear production metrics and operating rhythms.
* Improve throughput, yield, quality, and on-time delivery.
* Establish reliable capacity and labor planning.
* Identify and remove the biggest constraints to growth.
* Create a roadmap for automation, tooling, and production investment.
* Partner with Engineering to make our products easier, faster, and more cost-effective to manufacture.
* Establish a production operation that is safe, predictable, scalable, and ready for the next stage of growth.

**Compensation -**
130,000.00 - 160,000.00
 
 
**Benefits**

* Equity
* Medical, Dental, and Vision Benefits
* 401(k)
* Generous PTO
* Paid Holidays
* Daily Catered Lunches

*We are an equal opportunity employer that does not discriminate on the basis of race, national origin, gender, gender identity, sexual orientation, protected veteran status, disability, age, or other legally protected status.*
*Unusual Machines participates in E-Verify. E-Verify is an Internet-based system that compares information from an employee's Form I-9, Employment Eligibility Verification, to data from U.S. Department of Homeland Security and Social Security Administration records to confirm employment eligibility.*
*Candidates must be a US Citizen or permanent resident to be eligible for employment*

card.description:
Have you ever u sed the self-checkout? Played the slots at a Casino? Maybe you grabbed a drink from a vending machine or paid to park your car? If you’ve answered with a resounding “YES”, then you’ve done so with the aid of one of the 10 million devices installed by Crane Payment Innovations (CPI).
 
 
We make the technology that powers your everyday life, enabling more than 4 billion transactions every week in more than 143 currencies worldwide. From cash and coins to cards and mobile, we keep the world of payments moving with smart validation devices and business management software.
 
 
Headquartered in Malvern, PA, CPI is supported by: ~2,000 global associates, 6 manufacturing sites, more than 10 corporate offices and a global field service organization.
 
 
**What You’ll Be Doing**
We are seeking a strategic and influential CBS Director for the Service Business Unit to build and facilitate the business system that turns strategy into execution. This role owns how we execute and improve as a business. The Director will lead strategy deployment and the transformation review cadence, develop repeatable growth and operating processes, and use daily management and kaizen to improve cross-functional performance. You will build and facilitate the Service business system that connects strategy, growth, customer experience, service capabilities, and operational execution. Working through functional leaders and initiative owners, you will make priorities, progress, barriers, and improvement opportunities visible while preserving clear accountability for business results and execution.
 
 
**Key Responsibilities**

* Service business system: Design, implement, and continuously improve the management system used to translate Service Business Unit strategy into coordinated execution across functions.
* Strategy deployment: Facilitate the process for converting strategic priorities into defined initiatives, outcomes, measures, milestones, owners, and review routines.
* Transformation review cadence: Lead a consistent transformation review process that makes progress, risks, dependencies, decisions, and expected benefits visible to business leadership.
* Accountability model: Maintain clear governance, templates, and escalation paths while preserving accountability with initiative owners for delivering and reporting their results.
* Growth processes: Partner with Sales, Marketing, and Service leadership to develop a repeatable growth system spanning market mapping, target account selection, lead generation, account planning, opportunity qualification, funnel management, initiative launch, cross-functional readiness, benefit tracking, and revenue launch and ramp performance.
* Growth performance management: Establish practical measures and review routines that help leaders identify and address gaps in pipeline coverage, conversion, sales cycle time, launch performance, and progress against growth commitments.
* Operating processes: Standardize critical cross-functional processes where consistency, ownership, handoffs, or decision speed constrain execution.
* Daily management: Establish practical daily management routines, visual controls, performance measures, and escalation mechanisms that enable teams to identify and resolve issues at the appropriate level.
* Kaizen and continuous improvement: Identify, scope, facilitate, and sustain kaizen activity focused on meaningful cross-functional business priorities, using appropriate CBS tools and disciplined follow-through.

card.description:
**About Varda**
Low Earth orbit is open for business. Varda is accelerating the development of commercial space infrastructure, from in-orbit pharmaceutical processing to reliable and economical reentry capsules.
**Varda’s W-Series vehicles are built, designed, and operated by Varda in-house, including the pharmaceutical processing payloads, the capsules, the C-PICA heat shields, and the satellite buses.**
From life-saving pharmaceuticals to more powerful fiber optics, there is a world of products used on Earth today that can only be manufactured in space. Varda is accelerating innovation in the orbital economy by creating both the products and infrastructure needed so space can directly benefit life on Earth. Our mission is to expand the economic bounds of humankind.
 
 
Our team is uniquely suited to accomplishing this goal, with leadership and staff comprised of veterans from SpaceX, Blue Origin, major pharmaceutical companies and Silicon Valley. Varda was founded in January 2021 by Will Bruey and Delian Asparouhov with significant backing from world class investors including Khosla Ventures, Lux Capital, Founders Fund, Caffeinated Capital, General Catalyst, and Also Capital.
 
 
Varda is headquartered in El Segundo, California, where we have offices and a production facility where our vehicles, equipment, and materials are built, integrated, and tested. Varda also has offices in Washington, DC and Huntsville, AL.
 
 
Join Varda, and work to create a bustling in-space ecosystem.
 
 
**About This Role**
As the
**Principal Manufacturing Engineer (Payloads)**
at Varda, you will own the manufacturing and integration processes for the mission-critical payload systems that define what Varda's reentry capsules actually do in space. Varda's payloads — including pharmaceutical processing hardware, microgravity experiment modules, and government and commercial customer systems — represent the core value proposition of every mission. You will translate payload design requirements into production-ready assembly processes, develop rigorous work instructions, and work hands-on with technicians to ensure payloads are built, integrated, and verified to the highest standards of quality and cleanliness. This role demands both technical breadth and meticulous process discipline: you will interface with external payload customers, internal design teams, and the vehicle integration team to ensure every payload is ready to fly. If you are driven by the idea that what you manufacture will directly enable life-saving pharmaceuticals or cutting-edge scientific research in microgravity, this role is for you.
 
 
**Responsibilities**

* Own end-to-end manufacturing and assembly processes for Varda payload systems, including pharmaceutical processing hardware, experiment modules, and customer-furnished payload equipment
* Develop and maintain detailed work instructions, assembly travelers, process specifications, and acceptance test procedures for payload fabrication and integration operations
* Serve as the primary manufacturing interface for payload customers, translating customer requirements and ICD (Interface Control Document) constraints into executable production processes
* Implement contamination control, cleanliness, and handling protocols appropriate for sensitive payload hardware, including pharmaceutical-grade and precision optical components
* Collaborate with payload design engineers to provide DFM and DFA feedback on assembly accessibility, connector placement, thermal interface design, and testability
* Define and execute payload acceptance testing, functional verification checkouts, and pre-integration inspections; maintain complete and traceable build records
* Lead root cause analysis and corrective actions for payload non-conformances; coordinate MRB dispositions with design engineering and, where applicable, payload customers
* Coordinate payload integration milestones with the vehicle integration team, ensuring payload readiness gates align with overall vehicle build schedule

**Basic Qualifications**

* B.S. in Mechanical, Biomedical Engineering, or a related discipline, with consideration given to equivalent professional experience (typically 6–10+ years)
* 6+ years of experience manufacturing or integrating complex and compact electromechanical assemblies, scientific instruments, or payload systems in aerospace, defense, biomedical, or research environments
* Demonstrated experience building and integrating precision hardware to tight tolerances and exacting cleanliness requirements
* Ability to read and interpret engineering drawings, ICDs, and assembly models; familiarity with GD&T and interface requirement management
* Experience developing and executing assembly procedures and acceptance test plans for multi-functional hardware assemblies
* Strong written and verbal communication skills; comfortable interfacing directly with customers and cross-functional internal teams
* Must be physically able to regularly lift 25 lbs., bend, stoop, and stand for extended periods while working directly with flight hardware

**Preferred Skills And Experience**

* M.S. degree in Mechanical engineering specialized in Fluid Mechanics, Biomedical Engineering, or related discipline
* Experience manufacturing or integrating spacecraft payloads, scientific instruments, or hosted payload modules for LEO, GEO, or deep space missions
* Familiarity with pharmaceutical or bioprocessing hardware manufacturing requirements, including GMP considerations and contamination control protocols relevant to in-space drug manufacturing
* Background managing payload customer relationships from hardware delivery through integration, verification, and launch readiness
* Experience with ICD management and interface verification processes for payload-to-spacecraft integration
* Knowledge of microgravity experiment hardware design considerations and their manufacturing implications
* Familiarity with environmental testing (thermal vacuum, vibration, shock) as it applies to payload hardware acceptance and qualification
* Experience working in or adjacent to a cleanroom environment (ISO Class 7 or better) for integration of sensitive flight payloads
* Prior work at a company developing commercial space services with a direct end-user product — pharmaceutical, government, or research — where manufacturing quality directly impacted mission outcome

Pay Range
 
 

* Salary Range: $181,913 - $262,763/per year
* This role is on-site in El Segundo, CA
* Leveling and base salary is determined by job-related skills, education level, experience level, and job performance
* You will be eligible for incentives in the form of stock options and/or long-term cash awards

ITAR Requirements
 
 
Varda, like all employers, must ensure that its employees working in the United States are lawfully authorized to work in the U.S. Additionally, our employees are exposed to and have access to certain export-controlled items. Because our employees are provided access to export-controlled items, our policy is to only hire “U.S. persons” who are permitted to have access to our technology without an export license.
 
 
“US person” means: U.S. citizen, U.S. lawful permanent resident, or protected individual as defined by 8 U.S.C. 1324b(a)(3) (i.e., individual admitted to the U.S. as a refugee or granted asylum).

Varda Space Industries, Inc. participates in the U.S. Department of Homeland Security E-Verify program. The E-Verify program is an Internet-based employment eligibility verification system operated by the U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services. Learn more about the E-Verify program.

Candidates and employees are always evaluated based on merit, qualifications, and performance. **Who we are?**
As the world's largest organization of board-certified pathologists and leading provider of laboratory accreditation and proficiency testing programs, the College of American Pathologists (CAP) serves patients, pathologists, and the public by fostering and advocating excellence in the practice of pathology and laboratory medicine worldwide.
 
 
**Our Culture**

* CAP provides its employees with an energetic and collaborative work environment and encourage opportunities to further develop their skills—offering reimbursement for educational programs and participation in events that enhance your skills
* We offer a generous compensation and benefits package, 401K, and more -- visit Careers at the CAP for more details

Brief Description
 
 
The Director, Supply Chain Continuous Improvement is accountable for optimizing the end-to-end flow of work across the Supply Chain & Logistics function, including order management, procurement, planning, fulfillment, distribution, and logistics, from order receipt through customer delivery. The role streamlines and simplifies work, establishes process ownership and decision rights, clarifies roles and responsibilities, designs reliable handovers, and improves on-time delivery and temperature integrity through data, cross-functional leadership, and employee coaching.
 
 
Specific Duties
 
 

* Provides enterprise-wide matrix leadership to process owners, functional leaders, operations managers, and cross-functional transformation teams.
* Establishes accountability for outcomes, milestones, financial benefits, risk mitigation, and sustainment across a portfolio of strategic initiatives.
* Coaches senior leaders, managers, professional staff, and frontline employees in Lean, Lean Six Sigma, structured problem solving, change leadership, and daily management.
* May lead direct reports, contractors, consultants, or dedicated project resources as the transformation portfolio evolves.
* Develop and execute a multi-year Supply Chain & Logistics continuous improvement and operational excellence strategy aligned with enterprise customer, financial, quality, and service objectives.
* Own the Supply Chain & Logistics transformation portfolio: identify opportunities, size value, prioritize initiatives, define resource requirements, and govern delivery to scope, schedule, budget, risk, and targeted benefits.
* Lead end-to-end supply chain value-stream redesign across order management, procurement, planning, fulfillment, distribution, logistics, customer service, quality, and enabling functions.
* Establish process ownership, decision rights, escalation paths, governance forums, RACI frameworks, standard work, controls, and reliable handovers.
* Create an enterprise performance-management system and single source of truth for OTIF, temperature excursions, productivity, cost, handover defects, and customer-impact measures.
* Build executive-ready business cases for process, automation, analytics, and technology investments; partner with Finance to validate baselines, track realized value, and prevent benefit leakage.
* Lead complex Lean, A3, kaizen, root-cause analysis, and problem-solving initiatives that resolve systemic constraints and deliver sustained results.
* Sponsor digital process improvement using D365, WMS, TMS, workflow automation, Power BI/Tableau, and other enterprise platforms where appropriate.
* Build organizational capability through leader standard work, training, coaching, certification pathways, communities of practice, and succession development.
* Lead change-management and stakeholder-engagement plans that drive adoption, accountability, and sustained behavioral change.
* Partner with Quality, Customer Service, Supply Chain, IT, Finance, Human Resources, cold-packaging teams, suppliers, technology partners, and external carriers.
* Present portfolio performance, financial impact, risks, decisions, and recommendations to executive leadership and governance forums.

Source of Supervision
 
 
The Director, Supply Chain Continuous Improvement is a seasoned supply chain and operations excellence leader accountable for creating measurable enterprise value by improving the end-to-end flow of work across Supply Chain & Logistics and the broader value chain, from order receipt through customer delivery. This role owns the continuous improvement operating system and process governance for Supply Chain & Logistics, while leading a portfolio of high-impact cross-functional initiatives that improve customer experience, service reliability, quality, temperature integrity, productivity, working capital, and cost. **Become a part of our caring community**
=========================================

Humana is committed to helping people achieve their best health by delivering innovative technology solutions that enable exceptional member and provider experiences.
 
 
The Director, Segment Quality Engineering is a strategic technology leader responsible for advancing quality engineering practices across a defined portion of Humana’s technology portfolio. Reporting to the AVP, Quality Engineering – Segment, this role will lead teams responsible for delivery quality, test automation, release readiness, and continuous improvement across multiple product and application teams.
 
 
This leader will work closely with Product, Engineering, Architecture, Platform, DevOps, and enterprise quality partners to embed quality throughout the software development lifecycle and improve release confidence, delivery speed, and production stability.

**Responsibilities**

 

* Lead quality engineering strategy and execution across a defined portfolio, domain, or segment.
* Lead and develop quality engineering managers, leads, engineers, and SDETs; drive organization design, talent growth, and team performance.
* Establish portfolio quality goals, KPIs, and governance to improve delivery quality, release readiness, and production stability.
* Embed built-in quality across planning, design, development, testing, and deployment.
* Oversee test strategy and execution across functional, integration, end-to-end, regression, and release validation.
* Own portfolio-level quality risk management, including defect trends, release concerns, environment issues, and cross-team dependencies.
* Drive automation-first practices and integrate quality signals, validation, and gates into CI/CD pipelines.
* Lead adoption of AI-enabled quality engineering capabilities and promote innovative practices that improve speed, coverage, and reliability.
* Sponsor modernization of quality frameworks, tooling, and test approaches for APIs, distributed systems, and cloud-native platforms.
* Oversee non-functional quality practices, including performance, resiliency, operational readiness, and security validation.
* Use metrics and production insights to drive continuous improvement, maturity, and investment priorities.
* Partner with segment and enterprise stakeholders to align execution with broader quality engineering strategy, standards, and reference architecture direction.
* Ensure responsible adoption of AI and compliance with applicable security, privacy, regulatory, and operational standards.

**Use your skills to make an impact**
=====================================

**Required Qualifications**

 

* Bachelor’s degree or equivalent experience.
* 10+ years of experience in software engineering, quality engineering, testing, or related technical disciplines.
* 5+ years of leadership experience managing quality engineering, test automation, or software delivery teams in large enterprise environments.
* Experience leading quality engineering execution across multiple agile teams or a complex application/product portfolio.
* Demonstrated success driving quality engineering modernization, including automation, tooling, process improvement, and metrics-driven execution.
* Strong understanding of Agile, DevOps, and CI/CD practices.
* Experience with API, UI, integration, regression, and end-to-end testing approaches.
* Familiarity with distributed systems and modern application architectures.
* Strong communication and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to influence cross-functional leaders.
* Experience working in matrixed organizations and leading geographically distributed teams.

**Preferred Qualifications**

 

* Experience in healthcare or another highly regulated industry.
* Familiarity with member, provider, digital experience, or enterprise platform domains.
* Experience with enterprise quality tools, test management platforms, and engineering lifecycle tools.
* Knowledge of microservices, APIs, event-driven systems, and cloud-native architectures.
* Experience supporting non-functional testing, including performance and resiliency.
* Exposure to AI-enabled quality engineering or intelligent automation capabilities.
* Familiarity with enterprise reference architecture principles, patterns, and standards in cloud, hybrid, on-premise, and SaaS environments.

**Success in this Role**

 

* In this role, success will be measured by:
* Improved release stability and delivery quality across the assigned portfolio.
* Reduced escaped defects and production incidents related to delivery quality.
* Increased automation adoption, regression reliability, and validation efficiency.
* Stronger integration of quality engineering into engineering workflows and CI/CD pipelines.
* Advancement of quality engineering maturity and consistent execution across teams.
* Positive stakeholder partnership and strong team engagement and development outcomes.

40

$156,600 - $215,400 per year

Learn more about what we offer at Humana.com and at CenterWell.com.

card.description:
**This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, which manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for a Vice President, Quality Control based in the United States.**
The Vice President, Quality Control will provide strategic leadership for a global laboratory network supporting clinical development and commercial manufacturing programs. Reporting to the Chief Quality Officer, this executive will define and implement an enterprise-wide Quality Control strategy, ensuring scientific excellence, regulatory compliance, reliable data, and timely product release. The role oversees a broad range of laboratory operations across multiple sites and product modalities, while driving standardization, digital transformation, and operational performance. Working closely with senior executives, strategic clients, and regulatory authorities, the successful candidate will influence investment decisions, strengthen inspection readiness, and protect continuity of supply. This is an opportunity to shape a high-performing global organization and make a meaningful contribution to product quality and patient safety.
 
 
Accountabilities
 
 

* Define and execute the global Quality Control strategy, operating model, and multi-year roadmap across sites, product modalities, and development stages. Establish consistent enterprise standards, governance structures, and decision-making responsibilities while accommodating justified site-specific requirements.
* Provide executive oversight of end-to-end Quality Control operations, including analytical, biochemical, biological, microbiological, raw-material, in-process, release, and stability testing, as well as environmental and utility monitoring. Ensure laboratory capacity, priorities, and execution support program milestones, product disposition, client commitments, and uninterrupted supply.
* Govern the analytical method lifecycle from early development through transfer, qualification, validation, comparability, continued performance verification, and retirement. Ensure testing strategies and specifications evolve appropriately throughout clinical development, process performance qualification, product launch, and commercial supply.
* Establish global expectations for current good manufacturing practice, applicable good laboratory practice principles, data governance and integrity, laboratory investigations, out-of-specification and out-of-trend management, corrective and preventive action effectiveness, change control, and audit readiness. Lead enterprise-level regulatory inspection strategies and responses to critical client audits.
* Drive the global laboratory digital and technology roadmap, including laboratory information management systems, electronic laboratory notebooks, laboratory execution systems, chromatography data systems, automation, advanced analytics, and instrument connectivity. Sponsor validated technology deployment, master-data governance, cybersecurity, and adoption to improve accuracy, efficiency, and cycle times.
* Lead enterprise capacity planning, capital investment prioritization, make-versus-buy decisions, laboratory footprint strategy, and oversight of external testing partners. Align resources and contingency plans with demand forecasts, technology transfers, new product introductions, and network resilience requirements.
* Establish enterprise performance metrics and management reviews covering testing and release timelines, lead times, invalid results, out-of-specification and out-of-trend rates, investigation cycle times, corrective and preventive action effectiveness, stability execution, method performance, cost, and productivity. Promote risk-based decision-making, Lean practices, and cross-site learning.
* Act as the senior Quality Control representative for strategic clients, regulatory authorities, and executive governance. Translate complex technical and compliance risks into clear business implications, negotiate scientifically sound solutions, and ensure commitments are realistic and consistently delivered.
* Build and lead a global organization through senior leaders. Develop organizational capabilities, succession plans, technical career paths, and communities of practice while fostering scientific rigor, transparency, accountability, inclusion, and proactive risk management.
* Lead escalations and coordinated responses to significant Quality Control events, laboratory constraints, data-integrity concerns, assay failures, method or specification issues, and testing disruptions. Make or recommend risk-based decisions regarding testing strategies, product impact, remediation, and continuity of supply.
* Perform additional responsibilities in support of the broader Global Quality strategy and organizational objectives.

**Requirements**

* Bachelor's degree in Chemistry, Biochemistry, Biology, Microbiology, Pharmaceutical Sciences, Engineering, or a related scientific discipline, with at least 15 years of progressive Quality Control experience in the pharmaceutical, biotechnology, or contract development and manufacturing organization (CDMO) sector; alternatively, a Master's degree with at least 10 years of relevant experience.
* At least 10 years of people-management experience, including a minimum of five years leading senior leaders with responsibility for multiple laboratories, sites, or functional areas.
* Demonstrated leadership of Quality Control operations across clinical development and commercial manufacturing, including analytical method transfer, qualification and validation, release and stability testing, microbiology, and environmental and utility monitoring.
* Proven experience managing global regulatory inspections and client audits, as well as complex out-of-specification, out-of-trend, data-integrity, and laboratory-compliance matters.
* Experience overseeing budgets, capital investment portfolios, headcount, laboratory capacity, external testing partners, and enterprise transformation initiatives within a complex, matrixed global organization.
* Strong executive communication, stakeholder-management, and client-facing skills, with the ability to communicate complex scientific and regulatory matters clearly and influence strategic decisions.
* An advanced scientific degree and/or a Master of Business Administration is preferred.
* Global leadership experience within a CDMO supporting biologics, vaccines, advanced therapies, or sterile manufacturing is highly desirable.
* Experience scaling Quality Control capabilities from clinical development through process performance qualification, product launch, and sustained commercial supply is an advantage.
* Working knowledge of relevant regulatory authorities, standards, and guidance, including the US Food and Drug Administration, European Medicines Agency, Medicines and Healthcare products Regulatory Agency, and Pharmaceuticals and Medical Devices Agency.
* Familiarity with International Council for Harmonisation guidelines Q2, Q5, Q6, Q9, Q10, and Q14; United States Pharmacopeia; European Pharmacopoeia; Japanese Pharmacopoeia; Title 21 of the Code of Federal Regulations Parts 210, 211, and 11; European Union Good Manufacturing Practice Annexes 1 and 11; and applicable data-integrity expectations.
* Experience implementing global laboratory information management systems and laboratory digitalization and automation initiatives is preferred.
* Professional credentials from the American Society for Quality, along with Lean, Six Sigma, or equivalent quality and operational excellence training, are valued.

**Benefits**

* Annual salary range of $272,000–$325,000, with compensation determined by work location and relevant knowledge, skills, and experience.
* Medical, dental, vision, and prescription drug coverage.
* Health Savings Account option with company contributions.
* Industry-leading 401(k) savings plan.
* Insurance coverage and employee assistance programs.
* Wellness incentives designed to support overall health and well-being.
* Paid vacation, sick leave, and company holidays.
* A supportive environment that encourages personal and professional development.
* Global scope, with the role supporting sites worldwide. Compensation and benefits are governed by the location designated as the employee's home site.

card.title: Director of Quality
card.description:
**Director of Quality**

**Location:**
Springhill, TN or St. Louis, MO

**Position:**
Full-Time | Department Leadership Team

**Company Overview**

Our client is an established, growing manufacturing company specializing in custom-engineered components and solutions. With multiple manufacturing locations, the organization is committed to operational excellence, exceptional customer service, and continuous improvement.

**Position Overview**

We are seeking an experienced, results-driven Director of Quality to lead and oversee all aspects of quality management across a multi-location manufacturing organization.

This position serves as the company's senior quality leader, with overall responsibility for developing and executing the corporate quality strategy, maintaining the existing ISO 9001-certified Quality Management System, and leading the company's strategic initiative to achieve IATF 16949 certification.

The Director of Quality will provide leadership, direction, and professional development to all Quality Department personnel, including Quality Engineers, Quality Technicians, and future plant-level Quality Leaders.

The ideal candidate will have extensive manufacturing quality experience, strong leadership capabilities, and a proven track record of developing quality systems, improving operational performance, and building high-performing teams.

**Duties & Responsibilities**

**Quality Leadership & Management**

* Provide company-wide leadership and oversight of all quality-related activities across the organization's manufacturing operations.
* Lead, mentor, develop, and manage the corporate Quality Department, including Quality Engineers, Quality Technicians, and future plant-level Quality Leaders.
* Establish and execute the company's quality strategy, objectives, policies, and performance standards.
* Foster a proactive culture of quality, accountability, problem-solving, and continuous improvement throughout the organization.
* Partner with Operations, Engineering, Sales, Supply Chain, and executive leadership to ensure quality objectives align with business and customer requirements.
* Develop organizational capabilities, staffing plans, and employee training programs to support current operations and future growth.

**Quality Management Systems & Certification**

* Maintain and continuously improve the company's existing ISO 9001-certified Quality Management System, ensuring ongoing compliance, audit readiness, and successful maintenance of current certification.
* Develop and manage a comprehensive IATF 16949 certification roadmap, including gap assessments, implementation milestones, resource requirements, training, internal audits, and certification readiness.
* Ensure the company's Quality Management System (QMS) is enhanced to satisfy IATF 16949 requirements and applicable customer-specific quality standards.
* Lead and execute the company's strategic initiative to achieve IATF 16949 certification within established timelines.
* Lead the development, implementation, standardization, and continuous improvement of quality systems and processes across all manufacturing locations.
* Oversee internal, external, customer, and certification audits, ensuring ongoing compliance and successful certification.
* Serve as, or provide leadership to, the company's Lead Auditor and internal audit teams.
* Ensure effective management of corrective and preventive actions, nonconformances, documentation, calibration, and quality records.
* Lead management reviews and ensure ongoing QMS effectiveness and organizational accountability.

**Quality Performance & Continuous Improvement**

* Establish, monitor, and drive improvements in company-wide Quality KPIs, including customer complaints, internal and external PPM, cost of poor quality, scrap, rework, and corrective action effectiveness.
* Develop and implement quality improvement initiatives designed to reduce defects, improve manufacturing performance, and strengthen customer satisfaction.
* Lead complex problem-solving and root cause investigations using methodologies such as 8D, 5-Why, Fishbone/Ishikawa Diagrams, FMEA, and statistical analysis.
* Utilize data-driven decision-making, statistical process control (SPC), and other quality tools to proactively identify risks and improvement opportunities.
* Collaborate with Operations and Engineering to establish effective process controls, inspection standards, and preventive quality measures.
* Oversee product nonconformance management, containment, material disposition, and corrective action activities.

**Customer & Supplier Quality**

* Serve as the senior quality representative for key customer relationships, audits, escalations, and quality-related concerns.
* Ensure timely, professional resolution of customer complaints and implementation of sustainable corrective actions.
* Manage the Production Part Approval Process (PPAP), working closely with internal Quality and Business Development teams to ensure timely completion of customer approvals and achievement of new business launch schedules.
* Oversee Advanced Product Quality Planning (APQP) activities and ensure compliance with customer-specific quality requirements.
* Partner with Supply Chain and Purchasing to establish supplier quality expectations, manage supplier performance, and resolve supplier-related quality issues.
* Support new customer onboarding, new product launches, and manufacturing process changes to ensure quality requirements are achieved.
* Build strong relationships with customers, suppliers, and internal stakeholders to continuously improve quality performance.

**Strategic & Operational Responsibilities**

* Develop and execute long-term quality improvement plans aligned with the organization's growth objectives.
* Establish standardized quality processes, reporting, and best practices across all manufacturing locations.
* Support business expansion, new manufacturing capabilities, and potential acquisitions through quality system assessments and integration.
* Evaluate and recommend investments in inspection equipment, measurement technology, automation, and quality management systems.
* Prepare and present quality performance reports, improvement plans, certification progress, and key initiatives to executive leadership.
* Promote a safe work environment and ensure quality-related activities support company safety standards.
* Perform other quality-related leadership responsibilities as required.

**Experience & Education Requirements**

**Required Qualifications**

* Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Quality Management, Manufacturing, or a related technical field, or an equivalent combination of education and significant manufacturing quality leadership experience.
* Minimum of 8–10 years of progressive experience in manufacturing quality, including at least 3–5 years in a quality management or leadership position.
* Demonstrated experience leading and developing Quality Engineers, Quality Technicians, and/or plant-level quality personnel.
* Strong working knowledge of ISO 9001 and IATF 16949 Quality Management Systems, implementation, auditing, and compliance requirements.
* Demonstrated experience implementing or maintaining ISO 9001-certified Quality Management Systems.
* Experience supporting or leading IATF 16949 implementation, certification preparation, or certification audits.
* Lead Auditor experience with ISO 9001 or IATF 16949.
* Proven success improving quality performance, reducing defects, managing customer complaints, and implementing effective corrective actions.
* Strong knowledge of APQP, PPAP, FMEA, SPC, MSA, 8D, and root cause analysis methodologies.
* Experience managing customer and third-party quality audits.
* Excellent leadership, communication, organizational, analytical, and problem-solving skills.
* Proficiency with Microsoft Office applications, ERP/MRP systems, and quality-related software.
* Ability and willingness to travel between manufacturing locations and customer or supplier facilities as necessary.
* Must be physically based in the Nashville, TN, or St. Louis, MO, metropolitan area.

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Previous experience successfully leading an organization through IATF 16949 certification.
* Experience in automotive manufacturing, converting, or the production of engineered components and materials.
* Experience overseeing quality functions across multiple manufacturing facilities.
* ASQ Certified Manager of Quality/Organizational Excellence (CMQ/OE), Certified Quality Engineer (CQE), or Certified Quality Auditor (CQA).
* Six Sigma Green Belt or Black Belt certification.
* Experience implementing quality systems in a growing, multi-location manufacturing organization.
* Experience with supplier development, new product launches, and quality system integration.
* Bilingual English/Spanish communication skills are a plus.

**Leadership & Personal Attributes**

**The successful candidate will demonstrate:**

* A strong sense of ownership, accountability, and personal integrity.
* A hands-on, proactive leadership style with the ability to develop and inspire teams.
* The ability to balance strategic leadership with practical, day-to-day problem-solving.
* Strong customer focus and a commitment to delivering exceptional quality.
* An analytical, data-driven mindset with a passion for continuous improvement.
* Excellent interpersonal skills and the ability to collaborate effectively across all levels of the organization.
* A forward-thinking attitude, strong work ethic, and willingness to challenge existing processes to achieve better results.
* A commitment to operational excellence, customer satisfaction, and organizational success.
